title: Polity and Administrative Structure of Bihar

blocks.content: Covers Bihar's state government framework and its current political leadership — this chapter includes recent developments through mid-2026, so cross-check the current officeholders against a live source close to your exam date, since state political leadership can change.

Bihar has a bicameral state legislature — one of only a handful of Indian states to retain both a directly-elected Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and an indirectly-constituted Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad), a structural distinction worth remembering since most Indian states have moved to a unicameral system. The Legislative Assembly has 243 elected members, while the Legislative Council's composition draws from a mix of election by MLAs, local bodies, teachers' and graduates' constituencies, and Governor nominations, in keeping with the general constitutional design for state legislative councils across India.

As of writing, Bihar's political leadership reflects a significant and recent transition. The 2025 Bihar Legislative Assembly election, held in November 2025, delivered a landslide victory to the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA), which won roughly 202 of the 243 seats. Nitish Kumar, leader of the Janata Dal (United), was sworn in as Chief Minister for a tenth term on 1 December 2025, with Samrat Choudhary and Vijay Kumar Sinha of the BJP serving as his Deputy Chief Ministers. However, in a major subsequent development, Nitish Kumar moved to the Rajya Sabha (the upper house of Parliament) in March 2026 and resigned as Chief Minister; Samrat Choudhary was sworn in as Bihar's 24th Chief Minister on 15 April 2026, with Vijay Kumar Chaudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav taking over as his Deputy Chief Ministers. Given how recent and significant this transition is, candidates should treat these names as current at the time of writing and verify them against the latest official source immediately before any exam.

This political transition sits atop a state administrative structure that otherwise follows the standard Indian pattern: a Governor as constitutional head (appointed by the President of India), a Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister exercising actual executive authority, and a permanent civil service and district administration (headed by District Magistrates/Collectors) implementing policy on the ground across the state's 38 districts and nine administrative divisions.

items: Bihar Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) — the directly elected lower house, with 243 members, elected from single-member constituencies for a five-year term (subject to earlier dissolution).

Bihar Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) — the upper house, constituted through a mix of election by MLAs, election by local bodies, election by registered graduates and teachers within defined constituencies, and nomination by the Governor; members serve staggered six-year terms, with the Council itself a permanent body (never fully dissolved).

Bihar is one of only six Indian states (alongside Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh) to currently retain a Legislative Council — a frequently tested comparative fact.

The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and the Chairman of the Legislative Council preside over their respective houses; as of the 18th Assembly (constituted following the 2025 election), Prem Kumar has served as Speaker.
The Governor of Bihar is the constitutional/nominal head of state, appointed by the President of India; Syed Ata Hasnain has served in this role in the recent period covered by this book.

The Chief Minister, as the leader commanding a majority in the Legislative Assembly, heads the Council of Ministers and exercises the state's actual executive authority, supported by a Council of Ministers holding various departmental portfolios.

The state's permanent bureaucracy is headed by the Chief Secretary, with each of Bihar's 38 districts administered by a District Magistrate/Collector responsible for general administration, law and order, and revenue matters within their jurisdiction.
Bihar sends representatives to the Parliament of India through seats in both the Lok Sabha (directly elected) and the Rajya Sabha (elected by the state's Legislative Assembly members).

November 2025 — Bihar Legislative Assembly election held; the BJP-led NDA won a landslide victory with approximately 202 of 243 seats, while the RJD-led Mahagathbandhan (Grand Alliance) secured a much smaller share of seats.

1 December 2025 — Nitish Kumar sworn in as Chief Minister of Bihar for a tenth term, with Samrat Choudhary and Vijay Kumar Sinha as Deputy Chief Ministers, marking the formal constitution of the 18th Bihar Legislative Assembly.
March 2026 — Nitish Kumar was elected to the Rajya Sabha, prompting his resignation as Chief Minister shortly afterward.

15 April 2026 — Samrat Choudhary sworn in as the 24th Chief Minister of Bihar, with Vijay Kumar Chaudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav as his Deputy Chief Ministers, continuing the NDA's governing coalition of the BJP, JD(U), and smaller allied parties.

Panchayati Raj Institutions — a three-tier rural local governance system (Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad) operates across Bihar's rural areas, following the pattern established under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment; Bihar has been noted for a relatively high proportion of women's representation in Panchayati Raj bodies due to reservation policy.

Urban local bodies — Municipal Corporations (including the Patna Municipal Corporation), Municipal Councils, and Nagar Panchayats govern Bihar's urban areas under the framework of the 74th Constitutional Amendment.

The Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) is the state's constitutional body responsible for conducting recruitment examinations for state civil service and other government posts, functioning analogously to the UPSC at the central level.

Exam Tip

• Bihar's bicameral legislature (one of only six states with a Legislative Council) is a frequently tested comparative-polity fact — know the other five states in this category as well.

• This chapter covers a genuinely fast-moving current-affairs situation — the Nitish Kumar-to-Samrat Choudhary transition in April 2026 is very recent, so verify all named officeholders against a current source immediately before your exam rather than relying solely on this book's snapshot.

• The distinction between the November 2025 election result (NDA landslide, Nitish Kumar as CM) and the subsequent April 2026 leadership change (Samrat Choudhary as CM) is worth understanding as two separate, sequential events rather than a single fact.

blocks.content: A. Unicameral, with only a Legislative Assembly
B. Bicameral, with both a Legislative Assembly and a Legislative Council
D. Merged with the Lok Sabha
Answer: Bicameral, with both a Legislative Assembly and a Legislative Council
